**Post-Market Brief — Thursday, 5 November 2026**

- _Generated by cron #23 `agentic-post-market-brief` (fire scheduled 22:30 ET, 2026-11-05). Cash-session data is settled (as of 16:00 ET). After-hours prints are the final 20:00 ET postmarket tape.
- Futures and Asia indices are live as of **00:10–00:21 ET, Fri 6 Nov**._

---

**TL;DR**

- US equities suffered their worst session since the April 2025 tariff crash:
- the **S&P 500 fell 4.36% to 7,353.73**, the **Nasdaq Composite dropped 5.52% to 24,315.00** (confirming a technical correction, 10%+ below its 6 Oct record close), and the Dow lost 1,833 points (-3.44%) to 51,523.06.
- The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell **-12.2%** — its worst day since March 2020 — and roughly **$3 trillion** of S&P 500 market value was erased (Nasdaq-100 alone:
- -6.4%, a record $2.3tn).

- The catalyst is a **24-hour reversal in how the market prices one variable** — the Democratic sweep of both chambers in the 3 November midterms.
- On Wednesday, "Democratic limits on data-centre construction" was read as *good* for the hyperscalers that own scarce compute (MSFT +6.7%, AMZN +6.1%).
- On Thursday the same fact was repriced as *bad for the entire AI build-out*, and the suppliers were liquidated:
- NVDA -9.26%, AMD -17.26%, MU -17.46%, LRCX -16.36%, AVGO -10.43%, TSM -10.78%.

- Two caveats matter for how you read this. First, **the selloff is a political reprice, not an earnings event** — almost none of these names reported.
- Second, **the tape is not capitulated**:
- the equity put/call ratio closed at **0.44** (not elevated), and the after-hours session was bid, with SPY +0.17% and the semiconductor complex recovering 2–6% off the lows.
- The washout may be incomplete rather than finished.

- Overnight is worse, not better: the **Nikkei is -5.77%** and the **Kospi -5.13%** after a circuit breaker, the **Taiex -6.89%**.
- Hang Seng is the outlier at **+2.49%** as money rotated into discounted Chinese internet names.

- **The single most important item on the calendar is Friday 08:30 ET: the October Employment Situation (payrolls consensus +65K vs +29K prior) —
- landing into a 28.18 VIX and a market that closed below its 200-day moving average.**

- **Reading the table.** The watchlist held up *better* than the market (mega-caps -1.5% to -9.3% versus Nasdaq -5.5%), which is the point:
- the damage was concentrated in the AI *supply* chain, and the *buyers* of that supply — MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN — fell less than the index.
- NVDA closed essentially on its low (181.60 vs a 181.46 low) and lost roughly **$400bn of market value** in the process, the single heaviest drag on the S&P.
- AAPL was the relative winner at -1.53%. The two non-equity legs worked as designed: **GLD +0.81% and TLT +0.21%**, with the 10-year yield down 5.7 bp.

**Watchlist-relevant news**

- **The capex maths is the actual story.** For the three watchlist hyperscalers, Q3 2026 capex
- against operating cash flow: **Microsoft $39.4bn / $58.0bn ($0.68 per $1)**; **Alphabet $51.4bn / $42.3bn ($1.21 per $1)**; **Amazon $77.3bn / $42.4bn ($1.82 per $1)**.
- Together the four largest spenders (incl. Meta) spent ~$202bn against ~$175bn of operating cash flow — **$1.15 for every dollar**, and all four guided to spend more.
- On Amazon's trailing twelve months, free cash flow is **-$42.4bn**.

- **Buybacks are being funded out.** Combined buybacks for GOOGL, AMZN, META, MSFT and ORCL fell to
- **$4.4bn in Q3** — the lowest since Q3 2017, and down 90% from the Q4 2021 peak. Cash once allocated to repurchases is going into data centres.
- Combined 2026 capex for the group is tracking to ~$800bn; analysts project >$1.2tn in 2027.

- **Wednesday's trade was the mirror image.** On 4 Nov the same midterms produced MSFT +6.7%,
- AMZN +6.1%, GOOGL +3% on the thesis that constrained new construction *helps* incumbents with scarce compute (Dan Ives: the outcome is a "big hurdle for AI buildout").
- Thursday repriced the variable in the opposite direction — for everyone.

- **No watchlist name reports on Friday 6 November.** The mega-cap earnings week starts Monday
9 November (Apple, Palantir, and others).

**After-hours earnings reactions**

- All four of the marquee reports on Thursday night moved on **guidance**, not on the reported quarter —
- the same day the market was repricing the *cost* of building AI rather than the *revenue* of it.

**Up:**

- **FROG +21.95%** — Q3 revenue +31% to $179.2m, cloud revenue +60%. FY26 guidance raised to
adjusted EPS $1.14–1.16 on revenue $680–682m, versus consensus of $0.98 / $651.9m.

- **NET +14.57%** — Q3 revenue +39% to $782.5m, the company's fastest growth in nearly four years.
Q4 guidance of $0.43 adjusted EPS on $845–846m revenue, versus consensus $0.38 / $798m.

- **ABNB +11.02%** — Q3 revenue +19% to $4.9bn; adjusted EPS $3.16 versus $2.85 consensus; 2026
outlook raised; $12bn buyback added.

**Down:**

- **DKNG -22.24%** — Q3 revenue $1.33bn (+16%) versus a $1.40bn estimate; adjusted loss of $0.94
versus a $0.39 loss expected; sportsbook revenue $784m versus $811.8m consensus. FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance cut to $175–275m on higher spend on its new Predictions offering.

- **TEAM -15.98%**, **NTRA -16.43%**, **FIVN -21.12%**, **IRTC -14.74%**, **GH -10.39%**,
**XRAY -14.55%** — reported without a sourced catalyst detail.

- **LYFT -8.99%** — record gross bookings of $5.6bn (+17%), but results included a $117.9m impact
from legal, tax and regulatory reserve changes.

- Also worth flagging from the tape: **AAOI -7.61%** and **ELPW -14.18%** after hours —
- both optical/networking names already hit hard in the cash session, so the AI-supply-chain de-rating continued into the evening for the smaller names.

- below their 200-day moving averages, is the condition for a second leg down;
- a soft print (below ~50K) hands the shorts back their P&L and the after-hours semiconductor bid gets tested.

- and it is down ~31% from its 52-week high and ~16% on the week.

- Tests: the Nov 10 CPI, any state preemption or federal permitting action, and whether hyperscaler capex guidance actually changes in the 9–13 November earnings run.

MSFT $0.68, Alphabet $1.21, Amazon $1.82. Track it at each hyperscaler print.

cost of data-centre debt; Reuters reported the curve bull-steepening with the short end down 12 bp.

**Caveats carried into the numbers:**

- **Session volume is a post-close snapshot.** The closing auction consolidates after the bell, so
published volumes read slightly light; relative volume is computed against the 10-day average and is the more stable figure.

- **After-hours prints are the settled 20:00 ET postmarket tape**, re-confirmed at 00:20 ET. Thin
names (MAZE 76k, TGLS 60k, WK 108k) may carry wide spreads.

- **No European index levels are published.** The cash indices available at pull time were the
5 November closes; Europe's 6 November session had not settled, so only the Reuters futures reading (-0.6%) is cited.

- **Asian levels are live, not final** — Tokyo, Seoul and Taipei were still trading.
- **VIX/VXN closes are from the 16:15 ET index snapshot** and do not reflect overnight moves.
- **Two catalysts are recorded as unsourced** rather than inferred (see the gainers/losers tables);
where a catalyst could not be verified it is marked `*no catalyst sourced*`.
